@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: using standard unity features to accomplish exactly the goal of the feature isnt a hack in any sense of the word. this kind of accusatory wording is deeply concerning coming from a developer team.

my entire commission queue for avatar work has been completely uprooted because you guys couldnt wait until your replacement feature was released before breaking valuable avatar functionality.

you have the audacity to be actively suggesting that vrchat is a viable and reliable platform to support my livelihood with, and you cant warn us when core engine features are being removed?

Count me among those who relied on the ability to see features of my own avatar's head, including floppy ears and snout, among other things such as a visor or semi-transparent mask. Not only these features themselves but the visemes animating as I speak, the subtle movements when I activate expressions, and really feeling the interactions from others were all wonderful. I'm sad this is all gone and I hope you find a way to reinstate this functionality sooner than later.

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: Hey, thanks for working on this, especially the system to fix/replace the scale constraints. That's an important and very immersive feature that we would really like to have back. 

If you need help testing this, there are a lot of really talented creators here who would love to help you out. I hope to see the new system in a beta soon, and I look forward to 3.5.0!

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: It's not a hack if it was natively implemented into the engine. There's no real need for a new system if there was already one in place that most avatars were already using, so all that's really needed is to revert whatever was done to mess with first person features.

Also encouraging use of a system that you say may break in the future isn't really a good thing.
@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: ngl i'm kinda excited to see what that's teasing

I'll be sure to keep an eye out for your next Developer Update for more details. Shame that 5-10k uploaded avatars are now broken because this update wasn't backwards compatible. I should've known better than to hack this avatar-base together years ago!

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: Kinda blows that this new system wasn't released before scale constraints were disabled. It's left me and a lot of other avatar developers wondering how long it's going to take before 3.5.0 releases.

I'm pretty disappointed about this change and the lack of communication or care about it.
@{5fb4adefcbc50d6bb95d0dfd|full_name}: They kinda have a long history of not telling people things, or pushing updates without having suitable substitutes for things.

comments.mergedPostDetails:
Something changed with the latest update on "Scale Constraints".

On "local" avatars (the ones you see locally when you look down, not the ones in the mirrors) the head bone gets usually shrink down to "0.01" (which still is the case).

But if I use a "Scale Constraint" with this head bone as source, its object is not shrink down to "0.01" anymore.

Creators used this trick to make something like hats and helmets not visible locally but for others, so that the object doesn't get in the view all the time.

But right now it seems that the scaling of the "global" avatar is always used on your "local" avatar.

Repro:

Create an object on the root of the avatar, add "Parent Constraint" and "Scale Constraint" component to it, assign the head-bone of your avatar to their sources.

-> It doesn't scale down ingame anymore on your local avatar.

Expected:

"Scale Constraints" should scale with the bones of your "local" and "global" avatars separately.
comments.mergedPostTitle: Scale Constraints don't apply to "local" avatar anymore
comments.value: As VRC Roleplayers who use status Effects to show off what we are doing in character it's hard to 'see' in combat and causes nauseating experiences.

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: A new, more performant system is great and I look forward to it, but to break an existing feature of Unity PRIOR to implementing the new system is not a good way of handling it and it looks bad for VRC. It implies either you're out of touch with the needs of the users, don't care, or aren't capable of implementing an alternative in a timely manner.

There *are* jankier workaround, but unlike the existing system they get further into hacks potentially and come with downsides.

I had previously used Parent Constraints with sources of game objects which were children of Head, and they were scaled down local only. This is no longer the case now, so it does indeed seem that both Parent Constraints and Scale Constraints are effected in that way.

I am guessing this is a side-effect of the change "Constraint components are no longer added to mirrored avatars to help improve performance." in the patch notes: https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrchat-202342. In the patch notes there is some discussion about impact on avatars but I don't think this specific use case was mentioned?

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: The problem with Mirror Detection is that it does not detect cameras. Hiding features from first-person with this method would also hide it from cameras. Imagine hiding accessories, clothing and body parts from first-person, and then taking a selfie to see all of them missing.

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: What's the timeline for 3.5.0 VRC Devs quite honestly made alot of us upset in the VRC Roleplay community with this update.

The beta went too fast for us to discover this issue.

This workaround is a pain and has cost hundreds and perhaps thousands of dollars in commission money for VRC creators.

@{646eef1faa0f014bd4d9054e|full_name}: Hi flotts!

I believe they mean 'hack' more in the sense that it's disabling baseline functionality that wasn't intended to be disabled, not that anyone did anything wrong. We just can't generally guarantee something like this will continue to work when it wasn't intended behavior in the first place. (see also, the flying hack. I have to spend so much time making sure the flying hack still works...)

On the plus side, we'll be trying to restore the old functionality (as well as introduce something new, keep an eye on the dev updates) asap! We don't intentionally break community solutions when possible, but there was some tight deadlines approaching (as well as the holidays) and it couldn't be avoided this time around.

comments.mergedPostDetails:
I'll use Scale Constraints that follow the Head Bones of avatars so I can make avatar-to-avatar exclusive talking systems. i.e., a Pokemon exclusively talking to other Pokemon.

In a nutshell, FakeHead is mapped to the Humanoid Armature. MeshHead is constrainted to FakeHead's Rotation and Scale.

Suddenly after the VRChat Currency Update- Build 1389- the Scale Constraints just don't work. Rotation is still OK.

This is vital to some avatars, some not of my own. And I can't exactly disable this without redoing a bunch of commissions. Obviously from the image it renders some avatars nearly unusable.

Not sure what broke but I'm on the borderline of updating to 2022 Unity myself just to see if it changes at all. I got a feeling it's version crossover stuff.

comments.value: Was caught in the beta and pushed to live, honestly the old thread should probably be moved to bug reports https://vrchat.canny.io/open-beta/p/1381do-not-disable-the-scale-constraint-on-the-local-headbone

Hi everyone, we've reverted some changes around avatars that were causing issues and have made the decision to reintroduce this use case for scale constraints on avatars. We're still planning to provide a more performance friendly alternative for this at some point in the future - we'll go into some more detail about that in our next dev update!

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: Very positive about both of these things. Looking forward to seeing the 'full feature' when it's ready, and thankful that you're planning on reverting the changes that broke these use-cases until such a feature is ready.
@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: Thank you guys so much! Very much looking forward to this new feature you guys are working on!

@{6418adf793ca4d7f5ddb1c13|full_name}: Please be sure to consider the use cases outside of the most common ones (such as visible hats+hair or correcting such), when it comes to this and designing an alternative. Providing optimal alternatives for common cases is always good, but if it then robs functionality from other rarer creative uses, that would still be an unfortunate loss for very little gain. 

Discouraging excessive use of constraints makes sense, but I've never seen or heard of scale constraints being used in large numbers. They're used rarely, but when they are it's typically very deliberate. Unless there's some exceptional technical detail regarding them that I'm not aware of, it generally seems like a rather strange choice to single them out vs the rest.
@{5adfe287d198de6f75b8dc70|full_name}: it does work with cameras
@{5f2df4ecb923f7086bb15027|full_name}: That's amazing, thank you for the info!
